category: Owned channel / CRM / retention (dead list activation)
title: Jaipur D2C skincare brand turned a dead 84,000-email list into 20% of revenue and pulled blended CAC ₹640 → ₹510
content: SITUATION: A Jaipur D2C skincare brand at ₹38L/month had 71% of revenue from Meta and Google at a blended 2.1x ROAS, with CAC climbing to ₹640. It had quietly collected 84,000 emails and 31,000 WhatsApp opt-ins at checkout but sent nothing beyond order confirmations. Repeat-purchase rate sat at 9%. The list was the unworked asset. ACTION: We moved off a basic plugin to a proper ESP, cleaned to 62,000 deliverable contacts, and built three flows: an abandoned-cart WhatsApp sequence (Day 0/1/3), a post-delivery Day-12 replenishment nudge, and a Tuesday/Friday value email (skin routines, not just offers). We segmented by category and AOV and suppressed discount-only buyers from full-price launches to protect margin. OUTCOME: In 90 days email+WhatsApp drove ₹8.4L/month at near-zero variable cost — 20% of a now-₹42L month, mostly incremental. Abandoned-cart WhatsApp alone recovered ₹2.1L/month. Repeat rate rose 9% → 19%, and the cheap owned revenue pulled blended CAC ₹640 → ₹510.
lesson: The opt-ins you collect free at checkout are dormant revenue, not a database line-item — audit them before you add a rupee of ad spend. A 60k clean list with three working flows (abandoned-cart, replenishment, value content) out-earns lakhs of incremental paid, and because it carries near-zero variable cost it structurally lowers blended CAC instead of just buying more traffic. Build the flows before the broadcasts, and suppress discounters from full-price launches so retention doesn't quietly erode margin.
